Note: Tool catalog for the Remote Diagnostics window (gui\Gui.Core.psm1). Data only. Script = the base name the Run-*.bat launcher auto-detects (newest Name.v*.ps1, else Name.ps1). Inputs become arguments exactly as the launcher would pass them; Stdin inputs are never on a command line. Prompts and Results name the exact text the script prints (Source) - tests\gui\Test-GuiPromptContract.ps1 fails when a script no longer contains it. AllowedReadHost lists every Read-Host the GUI never reaches, with the reason. Prompt Kind: YesNo (a dialog, X sends Default), Text (a dialog with a text box, X sends an empty line), FromInput (sends the value of the named input, no dialog), Secret (sends the named Password input, never logged). Tool flags: Kind ChangesPC = the window asks for confirmation (Confirm text) before it runs; NoOutputFiles = the tool writes no output location, so a clean exit says Finished.

Tools.Title: Pull logs from THIS PC
Tools.Summary: Event logs, BSOD and crash dumps, GPU, print, network, startup and ESP checks from this PC, zipped into one file.

Inputs.Label: Hours to look back (1-168)
Include the full memory dump (MEMORY.DMP)
Output folder (empty = the logged-in user's Desktop\RemoteDiagLogs)

Results.Source: >>> COPY THIS FILE OFF THE MACHINE:
Results.Pattern: ^ >>> COPY THIS FILE OFF THE MACHINE: (?<v>.+)$

Tools.WarningText: The pull finished, but a step failed, so the output is incomplete (the script exits normally after a failed step).

AllowedReadHost.Why: hours prompt: the GUI always passes -Hours

AllowedReadHost.Contains: Include the full memory dump too?

AllowedReadHost.Why: press-Enter-to-close is skipped under redirected stdin

Tools.Title: Pull logs from ANOTHER PC
Tools.Summary: The same pull, over WinRM, from a PC where 'Enable remote diagnostics' was run. Needs a local admin account on that PC.
Tools.Notice: The other PC must have run 'Enable remote diagnostics' (it turns itself off after 48 hours). The password is sent to the script over its input only: it is never put on a command line, stored in a file or shown in the console, and the box is cleared when it is sent.

Inputs.Label: Computer name or IP
Local admin account on that PC (e.g. .\Admin or PC\Admin)
Password of that account (leave it blank if the account has no password and 'Enable remote diagnostics' was run there)
Hours to look back (1-168)
Include the full memory dump (MEMORY.DMP) from that PC (can be several GB over the network)
Output folder (empty = Public Desktop\RemoteDiagLogs on THIS PC)

Tools.WarningText: The pull finished, but a step failed, so the output is incomplete. A wrong user name or password, or remote diagnostics not enabled on that PC, fails every log like this (the script exits normally after a failed step).

Warnings.Pattern: ^  Checking log availability on target\.\.\. FAILED$
^  Establishing session for file transfer\.\.\. FAILED$

AllowedReadHost.Why: hours prompt: the GUI always passes -Hours
the GUI always passes -ComputerName (it is a required input)

AllowedReadHost.Contains: Include the full memory dump too?

AllowedReadHost.Why: interactive runs only: under redirected stdin the script reads the password with [Console]::In.ReadLine() instead (Read-Host -AsSecureString hangs there, spike S2)
press-Enter-to-close is skipped under redirected stdin

Tools.Title: Enable remote diagnostics on THIS PC
Tools.Summary: Opens WinRM and remote event-log access so another PC can pull logs. Turns itself off again after 48 hours.
Tools.Notice: Opens WinRM, remote event-log access and the remote registry on THIS PC, and relaxes the blank-password network-logon rule (LimitBlankPasswordUse). It is reverted automatically after 48 hours by a scheduled task; use 'Revert remote diagnostics now' to close it earlier.
Tools.Confirm: This opens WinRM, remote event-log access and the remote registry on this PC and relaxes the blank-password network-logon rule, so another PC can pull logs from it. It closes itself again after 48 hours (or earlier with 'Revert remote diagnostics now'). Run it?

AllowedReadHost.Why: press-Enter-to-close is skipped under redirected stdin

Tools.Title: Revert remote diagnostics now
Tools.Summary: Closes what 'Enable remote diagnostics' opened, before the 48-hour automatic revert.
Tools.Confirm: This closes WinRM, remote event-log access and the remote registry on this PC, restores the blank-password network-logon rule and cancels the automatic revert task. Run it?

Tools.Title: Deep persistence inventory
Tools.Summary: Everything that can start a script by itself, with hashes and copies of suspicious scripts. Slow, and the output is sensitive.
Tools.Notice: Slow (several minutes). The output holds PowerShell history and script copies: treat it as sensitive and do not leave it on a client's Desktop.

Inputs.Label: Output folder (empty = this account's Desktop)
Do not copy suspicious script files (samples)
Days of logon / RDP events (1-365)

Tools.Title: EFI partition usage
Tools.Summary: Who filled the EFI System Partition: Windows, HP or firmware capsules. Mounts it read-only and unmounts it after.

Tools.Title: Camera and startup check
Tools.Summary: Report only: camera devices, drivers, privacy settings, USB power and startup items. Changes nothing.
Tools.Notice: Report only (the launcher's R). The camera fixes (F) and DISM/sfc repair (A) change the PC and ask y/N per fix: use Run-CheckCameraAndStartup.bat for those.

AllowedReadHost.Why: fix questions: only asked with -Fix, which the GUI never passes

Tools.Title: Watch a print freeze
Tools.Summary: Start it, then print the job that freezes. Logs every change in the spooler, the app and the queues; saves events and crash reports when stopped.
Tools.Notice: Runs until the time is up or you press 'Stop and save'. Read-only apart from switching on the PrintService Operational log.

Inputs.Label: Minutes to watch (1-1440)
Program that freezes (process name)

Tools.Title: Switch printer WSD -> TCP/IP
Tools.Summary: Moves one print queue from a WSD port to a Standard TCP/IP port at the printer's IP, restarts the spooler and clears stuck jobs.
Tools.Notice: Changes this PC's print setup: the queue gets a new port, the spooler restarts and stuck jobs are cleared. Tick 'Dry run' first to see what it would do without changing anything. Note the change for the client.
Tools.Confirm: This switches the chosen print queue to a TCP/IP port on this PC, restarts the print spooler and clears stuck print jobs (nothing is changed when 'Dry run' is ticked). Run it?

Inputs.Label: Print queue on this PC (pick one or type its exact name)
Printer IP address (from its screen or a printed network page)
Inputs.PatternText: type four numbers separated by dots, for example 192.168.0.50.

Inputs.Label: New queue name (optional; empty = keep the same queue)
Also remove the old WSD port and duplicate queues if they are unused (it asks first)
Print a test page afterwards
Dry run: show what would happen, change nothing

Prompts.Source: Printer IP address (from its screen or a printed network page):
Prompts.Title: Printer IP address
Prompts.Message: The tool asks for the printer's IP address (from its screen or a printed network page). Closing this box sends an empty line and the tool stops.

Prompts.Source: Switch the queue to this port anyway? (y/N):
Prompts.Regex: ^Switch the queue to this port anyway\? \(y/N\):$
Prompts.Title: The printer does not answer
Prompts.Message: The printer does not answer on TCP 9100 (raw printing): wrong IP, printer off, or raw printing disabled. Switch the queue to this port anyway?

Prompts.Title: Remove the old queue?
Prompts.Message: The new queue is in place. Remove the old queue now?

Prompts.Title: Remove this queue?
Prompts.Message: This queue looks like an unused duplicate. Remove it?

Prompts.Title: Remove the unused WSD ports?
Prompts.Message: The ports listed in the console are no longer used by any queue. Remove them?

AllowedReadHost.Why: every use is the answer to one of the prompts above (the IP prompt is never reached: -IpAddress is required)
